title: Thesis Distillation: Investigating The Impact of Bias in NLP Models on Hate Speech Detection
findings: The paper investigated religion as a sensitive attribute for bias and fairness in hate speech detection. It found that language models exhibit social biases related to religious terms. The study evaluated the impact of removing these biases (representation, selection, overamplification) on model fairness. For example, results showed that debiasing methods had varying effects on fairness scores related to religion, sometimes improving and sometimes worsening them depending on the model and method used. A positive correlation was found between a proposed 'Systematic Offensive Stereotyping' (SOS) bias metric and social bias scores related to religion as measured by CrowS-Pairs.

measurement_description: The paper measured social bias (stereotypical associations) and fairness related to religious identity terms within the context of hate speech detection. This included representation bias, selection bias, and overamplification bias.
